public_rationale: NVIDIA’s annual figures are consistent with roughly 90% Data Center revenue. That does not settle the publication-date index weight or the claim that buyers immediately lose money installing the hardware. AWS’s positive operating income is relevant caution, but it cannot establish installation-level profitability. The compound claim remains unresolved.
limitations: The annual revenue comparison differs from the default quarterly scope.
Broad company or segment earnings cannot settle individual infrastructure returns.
An unknown accounting basis prevents a supported or contradicted money assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Data centers make up 90% of NVIDIA's revenue, so about 8% of the S&P 500's value comes from a company selling hardware to buyers who immediately lose money installing it.

statement.excerpt: Said data centers make up 90% of NVIDIA’s revenue, which means that 8% or so of the S&P 500’s value comes from a company that makes money selling hardware to people that immediately lose money on installing it.

from_speaker: 8% or so of the S&P 500’s value
people that immediately lose money on installing it
our_interpretation: Data centers means NVIDIA’s Data Center end-market revenue.
For the ongoing revenue assertion, the default comparison is the latest reported quarter before publication, ending January 25, 2026.
The index assertion concerns NVIDIA’s float-adjusted index weight around April 8, 2026, independently of its revenue mix.
The target interval encompasses that latest quarter and the publication-date market snapshot; it does not make every observation within the interval interchangeable.
The plain reading of immediate losses concerns buyers’ economics from installing the hardware. An initial capital payment is not itself proof of a loss.
No accounting basis or financial source is identified in the supplied claim, so the contract basis remains unknown.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable revenue data establish a share near 90%, contemporary index records establish a weight near 8%, and buyer-level records establish the asserted immediate installation-related losses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records materially contradict a percentage or demonstrate that the asserted generalization about buyers’ installation losses is false.

evidence.locator: Opening results paragraph; Data Center highlights
evidence.explanation: The release reports annual Data Center revenue of $193.7 billion, giving an annual share of about 89.7%. This supports the plausibility of the annual reading but does not resolve the complete claim or the contract’s unspecified accounting basis.
AWS reported positive segment operating income. This cautions against a broad loss-making-buyer interpretation, but segment income does not isolate returns on newly installed NVIDIA hardware.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A specified revenue period and basis, a contemporary index-provider weight, and comparable installation-level buyer economics.
